These decisions are in accord with our Constitution and General Regula.tions, and we recommend their approval.

th~

II. There is nothing unconstitutional in the adoption by a Lodge of
following resolution:"Resolved, That every application for dues being remitted must be made
in writing or in person hy. the delinquent himself, stating his. reasons for his
inability to comply with the ·financial requisitions of the laws of the Lodge."
Your committee are compelled to dissent from the foregoing decision for
the reason that the resolution under consideration modifies, or restricts, the
provisions of Sec. 11 of Art. III of Part III of the ConRtitution, the first
port.ion of which section reads as follows :-

./

Sro. 11. N~ Lodge shall expel a member for non-payment of hie dues;
but, in case any member shall have refused or negleetOO to . pay his regular
dues during a period of six months, he shall be notified by the Secretary that,
unle88 at the next stated meeting·either his dues be paid or sickness or inability
to pay be shown as the cause of such refusal or neglect, he will be suspended
from all the rights and privilei;ies of Masonry.
It is a well recognized pr(lviaion of law that the provisions of a Constitution can neither be extended nor restricted by legislation. The resolution
under consideration is, in effect, an attempt to restrict the application of the
following clause of the section above quoted, viz.:" Or aickne88 or inability be shown as the cause."
The Constitution provides no particular method by which the "inability
be shown," while the resolution says that it can be shown only "in writing or
in person" by the delinquent himself. We are of the opinion that, for this/
reason, the resolution is unconstitutional.
'

III. An application to a Lodge for permi88ion to form a new Lodge must
be accompanied by a proper dimit in the case of each brother signing the ap1;>lication. No one while a member of a Lodge should vote on his own application
to form a new Lodl(e.
We a~ee with the Grand Master so far as the foregoing decision relates to
·the propriety of a member voting on his own application for permi88ion to
form a new Lodge from a subdivision of the Lodge of which he is a member;
but, on the other hand, we know of no law or regulation in Masonry by which
a member who is present at a meeting, and is in good standing in his Lodge,
.can be arbitrarily deprived of the privilege of voting on any and every proposition which is submitted to the vote of the members of the Lodge.
IV.
ARMY LoooES.
Two applications have been received by me during the past six months
asking for dispensations to form Lodges among the soldiers enlisted from this
State.
A careful examination of the reports of various Grand Masters from 1861
to 1865 upon the so-called Army Lodges convinced me that for various
reaaonij it would not be for the best interests of the Craft to grant dispensations of such a character, at least until the Grand Lodge had determined the
manner and.method by which such diepene&tiona were to be granted.

I

854

Prooe.edinga of the

[Oct. 14;·

When the Philippines shall have come under the authority of the United
States and something of political and social permanency have been secured,
the location of Masonic Lodges in that far away land to assist in the uphuilding of the State and the elevatic.n of mankind will be the duty of this
great Order.
I refer this subject to you for your consideration and for such action as
may by you be deemed wise and proper for the future.
We commend the discretion of the Grand Master in {.efusing to issue
special dispensations for the organization of Army Lodges. An Army Lodge
is an anomaly in Masonry. Its meetings are held at any place where the exigencies of the military service ma.y cause a temporary encampment. If held
in our own coantry, such meetings are necessarily an invasion of ihe jurisdiction of other regularly constituted Lodges. During the clash of battle in our
late civil war, it sometimes ha.ppened that Army Lodges, with their charters ·
a.nd records, were swept from existence, and the unfortunate members of such
Lodges were thus deprived of membership, without dimits or other rticords to
show that they had received the degrees of Masonry in a regularly chartered
Masonic Lodge. We recommend that this Grand Lodge condemn, with
unqualified disapprobation, every effort, from any soarce, to revive the pernicious practice of issuing dispensations for the organization of any Lodges of
such a character.
Our Grand Master has wisely suggested that the time may speedily come
when it shall become our duty, as well as our privilege, to grant authority for
the organization of Masonic Lodges in the Philippine Islands. We shall
rejoice in the consummation of events tha.t lead up to so desirable and important an event in our history, confident that the wise discretion and sound
judgment of our Grand Master will enable him to solve the problems as may
thus confront him in such a manner as to reflect credit upon himself and to
redound to the honor a.nd prosperity of our beloved Fraternity.
Respectfully submitted.
EDWARD M. PRESTON,}

, Bro. HIRAM N. RuoXER, from the Committee on Jurisprudence,
presented the following :To the M. ·. W. ·. Grand Lodge of California :Bro. ORRIN STAPLES HENDERSON, of MoT11ing Star Lodge, No. 68, proposes
the following : Rer.olved, That immediately after adjournment of the annual session of the
Grand Lodge, the Grand Master shall apportion to himself and the Deputy
Grand Master, Senior and Junior Grand Wardens, meeting in consultation
such districts of the State as may be reasonably covered by themselves · and
that in such districts allotted to thbm they shall visit in an official capacity
such Lodges as may be within their respective'districts.

1898.]

Grand· Lodge of OalAfornin..

857

Your committee are of the opinion that, to thus divide the State into districts, would practically deny three-fourths of the Craft the hope of receiving
a visit from the Grand Master during the year. The Grand Master already
has his . specially appointed agents in the persons of the Inspectors to look
after 1.he welfare of the Lodges, and we question whether the interests of
Masonry would be additionally subserved by the proposed plan.
The Grand Lodge has very properly provided a fund for the contingent
expenses of the Grand Master. To make it obligatory that the other Grand
Officers above named shall do a share of the visiting should, in justice, require
an additional fund wherein the results would hardly justify the expenditure.
The adoption of this resolution would make it necessary for these Grand
Officers to visit officially every Lodge within their respective districts, and
would make the duties so onerous that we fear the requirement could not be
fulfilled. There is no reason why the Grand Master may not call upon the
Deputy Grand Master and the Grand Wardens to represent him on any
occasion of official duty when not convenient for him to attend in person.

It is with pleasure that your committee again report a marked improvement
in the accession of membership, and the steady increase throughout the juris·
diction in the number of degrees conferred b.y the subordinate Lodges. The
Craft has never, in its history, been in a more flourishing and prosperous condition in the jurisdiction of California.
For a number of years past, at each Convocation of this Body, your committee has been compelled, regretfully, to criticise, in many instances, the
manner of performing and the indifference shown in the discharge of the
duties of Maaters and Secretaries of subordinate Lodges in the prepa.ration
and forwarding to the Grand Secretary, returns of th1> condition of their
various Lodges; and, annually, upon the recommendation of your committ.ee,
this Grand Lodge has passed resolutions tending to effect improvement, if not
absolute perfection in this matter. The returns here presented show such
marked improvement, and the number of returns lfa,ble to censure being com·
pa.ratively so few, your committee is inclined to believe that its recommendations made in the past, a.nd the action of the Grand Lodge thereon, have been
effective, and we therefore recommend that in future, and until the further
order of this Grand Body, the Grand Secretary, as soon as he shall have forwarded to the Secretaries of subordinate Lodges, notify the Inspectors of the
several districts that such blanks have been so forwarded, and that: it shall
become the duty of each Inspector, when so notified, to impress upon the
Master and Secretary of each Lodp;e in his Distriet the neceesity of complying strictly with the requirements of the Constitution in that regard and
the instructions of the Grand Secretary ; this being the procedure heretofore
adopted.
All which is respectfully adopted.

Bro. ANDREW BROWN presented the following :
To the M. ·• W. •. Grand Lodge of California:-Hawaiian Lodge, No. 21, has ever been proud of and loyal in her allegiance
to this Grand Lodge. It is her desire to still remain so, as long as is possible.

870

J

Proceedings of thAJ

(Oct. 14,

The strong ties of the past, as well 11.11 the harmonious relations of ibe present,
tend to bind us to a continuance of that allegiance.
Since the Hawaiian Islands have become U. S. territory, issues in Ma.eonry
have arisen which prompt the members of Hawaiian Lodge, No. 21, to repair
to the parental Body, 11.11k questions and seek the advice of those w6ll skilled
in Masonic law. Bearing in mind that it is in the light of truth and justice,
and for our proper guidance', we respectfully ask the following questions ;Can Haivaiian Lodge, No. 21, continue, as at present, under the, jurisdiction of the Grand Lodge of California ?
·
We understand tha.t the formation of a Grand Lodge in these i~lands is
optional and not obligatory, and that it requires the co-operation of three
chartered Lodges to form a Grand Lodge. Is this correct!
In c11.11e action is taken by the other Lodges to form a local Grand Lodge,
without the concurrence and co·operation of Hawaiian, No. 21, will we be justified in refusing to be coerced by a Lodge which recognizes three blackballs,
and admits to Masonry candidates who are physically disqualified under' our
requirements?
As Hawaii has become a part of the United States, is it not necessary for
the Lodges here holding charters from foreign jurisdictions to relinquiah them
and come either under some United States jurisdiction or form a local Grand
Lodge!
In view of the desire of H11,waiian, No. 21, to remain under the Grand
Lodge of California and not join a local Grand Lodge, is it not to our interest,
in fact necessary, that we consent to the two foreign Lodges, viz.: Le Progre8
L'O~na and Pacific, coming under the American Juriadiction, WI we have
reason to believe such is their desire !
With reference to our Lodge property, we understand that the Temple is
the private property of Hawaiian, No. 21, the purely Masonic furniture only
being under the control of the Grand Lodge. Is this correct ?
These are some of the questions to which we desire answers, and we
respectfully suggest that they be referred to the Committee on Jurisprudence
for that purpose.

The reference was made as suggested.

Bro. CHARLES W. NUTTING presented the following report:To the M.'. W.'. Grand Lodge ofCJalifornia:-

Your committee, to whom was referred the report of the Grand Lecturer,
have had the same under consideration and report as follows : We realize the difficulties attendant upon a faithful diacharge of the duties
of the office of Grand Lecturer, and appreciate the painstaking earnestness and
zeal with which the present Grand Lecturer has labored during the past
Masonic year. We heartily coincide in the conclusion of the Grand Lecturer
that Inspectors who obstinately refuse to receive instruction from the properly
constituted authorities should be removed from office, and we are pleased
to note that such obstinacy is the exception and not the rule. We recommend the following : That so much of the report as refers to salary, duties, etc., be referred to
a special committee of three, with instruction to submit some feasible plan by
which uniformity of the work can be attained throughout the jurisdiction,
said committee to report at the next Annual Communication of this Grand
Lodge.
Tha.t so much of the report as relates to the. unsuitable condition of several
Lodge-rooms, be referred to the Grand Master.
All which is fraternally submitted.

· The Grand Lodge was called on at ten o'clock, the Grand Master
presiding.
After music by the choir, and prayer by the Grand Chaplain, the
minutes of the sessions of yesterday were read and approved.
Bro. JAHES B. STEVENS, from the Committee on Jurisprudence,
presented the following :To the M. ', W. •• Grand Lodge of California :your committ.ee, to whom was referred th~ several questions submitted by
Hawaiian Lodge, No. 21, beg to report that theyhave had the same under
consideration. The questions-came into our hands only last evening, and we
have not had the opportunity to give to them that careful review which their
importance demands.
Owing to the new problems of Masonic law and precedent arising out of
the conditions resulting from the acquisition of new territory by the United
States these questions are invested with international importance.
therefore respectfully ask that the questions be referred to our suc·
cessors, with the recommendation that they prepare a statement of their
answers at the earliest practicable date. That such answers, when agreed
upon by the committee, be submitted to the Grand Master for his consider&·
tion. If approved by him, they shall be forwarded to our brethren in Hawaii,
as the ruling and edict of this Grand Lodge.
Respectfully submitted.

Bro. ELMER 'E. STONE, from the Committee on Finance, presented
the following reports : To the M. '. W. '. Grand Lodge of Calijornio.:y our committee, to whom was referred the preamble and resolution offered
by Bro. Past Grand Master .ATKINSON, directing the Grand Treasurer of this

eral Fund of this Grand Lodge, have had the matter under advisement, and
believing that the financial interest of this Grand Lodge will be best subserved
by such exchange of funds, offer the follc,wing resolutions and recommend
their adoption :.....,Resolved, That the Grand Treasurer be and is hereby authorized to withdraw from the Reserve Fund the U. S. 4 per cent bonds of the par value of
$3950, and transfer the same to the General Fund of this Grand Lodge. Be it
further
ResolvM., That the Grand Treasurer be and is hereby instructed to transfer
and substitute in lieu thereto such other securities held by this Grand Lodge
as will be equivalent to the amount of $3950, for the purpose of maintaining
the Reserve Fund as required by General Regulation No. 3.

Your committee, to whom was referred the resolution offered by Bro.
CooK, directing that the sum of $3500 be transferred to the Charity Fund of
this Grand Lodge, to be used for the relief of indigent Masons, have given
the matter careful consideration, and in view of the fact that extraordinary
expenditures of money have been authorized by this Grand Lodge for the
ensuing Masonic year, and as we do not feel justified in making this appro·
priation, nor will the funds of this Grand Lodge warrant the expenditure of
said amount, we therefore recommend that said resolution be not adopted.
Fraternally submitted.

Your committee again call attention to the neglect of Secretaries of subordi·
nate Lodges not returning correct fares to San Francisco from their respective
places. Your committee have based their report on the limited first-class fare
to San Fr&ncisco and recommend that their action be approved.
Your committee offer the following re~oln tion and recommend its a<loption :

Ruolved, That there be levied upon the subordinate Lodges of this jurisdiction for the current fiscal year, in addition to the dues prescribed by the
Constitution, the sum of twenty (20) cents for each member borne upon the
respective rolls at the date of the annual reports. Said levy shall be made for
the Representative Fund, and shall be paid at the same time and in the manner
prescribed for the payment of the annual dues.
Your committee wish to express their thanks for the kindneeses and courtesies extended to them by the several representatives for promptly responding
with their help and information in adjusting the pay-roll of allowances.
All which is respectfully submitted.
ORRIN S. HENDERSON, }
